As a single ember left of a great fire, fed with straw, blazes up again, so with food his one remaining part blazed up: mind is made of food.

paraphrase: When a person departs, his speech merges into mind, mind into breath, breath into heat, and heat into the highest deity.

That which is the finest essence — this whole world has it as its self; that is the real; that is the self; that you are (tat tvam asi), Śvetaketu. 'Teach me further, sir.' 'So be it, dear one.' The refrain recurs at the close of each of the following illustrations (6.9.4 to 6.16.3; nine times in all).

Next the teaching of the self (ātmādeśa): the self is below, above... the self is all this. One who sees, thinks and understands thus delights in the self, plays with the self, couples with the self, has joy in the self; he becomes self-ruled (svarāṭ) and moves at will in all worlds; those who think otherwise are ruled by others and their worlds perish.

paraphrase: For one who sees thus, breath, hope, memory, space, heat, water, appearance and disappearance, food, strength, understanding, meditation, thought, intention, mind, speech, name, the mantras and rites all arise from the self. 'The one who sees does not see death, nor sickness, nor sorrow; he sees all and obtains all.' When food is pure, the mind (sattva) is pure; when the mind is pure, memory is firm; when memory is gained all the knots are loosened. To him whose stains were wiped away the blessed Sanatkumāra showed the far shore beyond darkness; they call him Skanda.

As people who do not know the field walk again and again over a hidden treasure of gold without finding it, so all creatures go daily to this world of brahman (in sleep) without finding it, for they are carried away by untruth. The self is in the heart (hṛdi ayam), hence the word 'heart' (hṛdayam).

paraphrase: Indra, before reaching the gods, sees the flaw: if the body is adorned the reflection is adorned, if blind blind, and it perishes with the body. He returns; after thirty-two more years he is taught: 'the one who moves about happy in dreams is the self'. He sees the flaw again: though untouched by the body's defects, the dream-self seems to be struck and chased, to feel pain and to weep.
